newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees devaluation decision in April-May'97.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees devaluation decision in April-May'97.

text.p: The earliest likely date for Hungary to make a decision on a potential cut in the rate of its monthly 1.2 percent preannounced crawling-peg devaluations is April or May 1997, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.

"If the government forecasts are justified and economic processes, especially inflation, go as we expect, there will be an opportunity to cut the rate in the second half of next year," State Secretary Tibor Draskovics told a news conference.
"We will have sufficient information about the processes for a decision in April, or May the earliest," he added. @
Hungary plans to cut inflation to 18 percent next year from a forecast 22 to 24 percent in 1996.
Hungary's monthly devaluation rate for this year is 1.2 percent. The government has recently decided that the maximum monthly devaluation rate in 1997 would be 1.2 percent.
Government and central bank officials said the rate was likely to remain 1.2 percent from January 1.
Draskovics admitted that Hungarians' expectations for next year's inflation rate are well above the government projection.
"If my wife tells me what she experienced in the food shop, her inflation expectations are of course above mine," he said. @

However, he added that people should not rely on their feelings about inflation as economic processes and the intentions of the market participants showed that the country had every chance to meet the 18 percent target.
"It must be clear, that not only the government expects a low inflation rate, but the intentions of entrepreneurs also do not underpin a higher (than 18 percent) rate," he added.
